newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia capital market strong in 1997 - seminar.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia capital market strong in 1997 - seminar.

text.p: An Indonesian economic seminar said it sees a good future for the country's capital market in 1997 despite falling prospects for the Asia-Pacific region as a whole, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

"Although predictions for the emerging markets of the Asia-Pacific are for a fall compared to this year...the Indonesian capital market will do better than other countries in the region," Rizal Ramli, director of the Econit economic think-tank, was quoted as saying.
He said increased interest rates in many OECD countries was one reason for weakening capital markets in the Asia-Pacific region.
Ramli said the main factor in Indonesia's relative strength would be a cooling off in the domestic economy next year which would lead to an increase in earnings per share of listed companies.
Ramli said, however, this growth was dependent on continued political stability.
"Further troubles such as the president's health or riots like those in July could lead to a fall in the index," Antara quoted him as saying.

The Indonesian stock market dipped sharply after riots in Jakarta in July, the worst for over twenty years. President Suharto's recent trip to Germany for a medical check-up also caused jitters on the Jakarta bourse.

William Belchere, head of Merrill Lynch's Asia Currency and Fixed Income Research in Singapore, was quoted as saying that Indonesian portfolio transactions for 1997 were expected to reach around $2.0 billion.
Transactions for 1996 were around $1.5 billion, he said.
